data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Coverage debt under the current batched criticism mechanism grows non-linearly with the size of accepted rival positions, causing a 'criticism starvation' phase where no rivals are retired after the system scales from 18 to ~60 rivals; implementing a tournament-based selection filter before the criticism phase is a necessary optimization to bound this debt.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the sandboxed simulation shows coverage debt growing linearly (O(N)) with rivalry size, the non-linear debt hypothesis is falsified.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If tournament-based selection reduces the diversity of accepted rivals below a functional threshold without proportionally increasing the retirement rate, the optimization is counterproductive.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A sandboxed Python simulation (simulation_mode sandboxed_python_v1) is proposed to test this: it initializes N rival positions (scaling N from 10 to 100) and models batched criticism where an argumentative_critic generates per-target warrants. In the naive model, the simulation calculates coverage debt as the ratio of generated warrants to attacked targets. In the optimized model, a tournament-selection mechanism reduces the active rivals to a K-sized batch before criticism. We hypothesize the naive model will show debt growing O(N^2) while the optimized model bounds it. We also propose a research fetch to https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popperian_critical_rationalism to inform the critic's validity gate logic.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
